chapter_title: Concerning the Body: It was constructed after the Pattern of the Universe
chapter_note: Overwhelmingly substrate chapter — the oldest body-cosmos correspondence teaching dominates. Teaching purity 0.967 with no editorial bridge, no exhortation, and negligible editorial fatigue. Gardner notes redaction from multiple sources/lessons, visible in the distinct teaching blocks: (1) body→cosmic structures (¶2-3), (2) five watches and their conflicts (¶5-16), (3) five body regions→cosmic rulers with ethical framing (¶17-24), (4) four body worlds with seven rulers each (¶25-29), (5) zodiac-body correspondences in two schemas (¶31-36), (6) numerical powers in the body (¶38-39). The ethical framing in ¶18-22 ('Whoever will master X resembles cosmic ruler Y') is the main editorial overlay — it wraps substrate body-cosmos mappings in application to the elect. The three dialogue frame paragraphs are minimal. This chapter preserves some of the most systematic body-cosmos correspondence teaching in the Kephalaia.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic scene-setting: 'the apostle is sitting down among the church in the midst of the congregation.' Institutional vocabulary ('church', 'congregation') scores 19.23. No cosmological content.

paragraphs.core_text: This whole universe, above and below, reflects the pattern of the human body; as the formation of this body of flesh accords to the pattern of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The thesis statement of the chapter's body-cosmos correspondence teaching. Microcosm = macrocosm stated as structural principle. Both sides of the mapping (universe, body) stay within the cosmic system. No frame formula, no attribution.

paragraphs.core_text: Its head is like the first-fruits of the five garments. And, from its neck down to the site of its heart, it resembles the pattern of the ten firmaments. And again, the heart accords to the wheel of the rotating sphere. And, from its heart down to its intestines (?), is like this atmosphere that extends from the sphere down to the earth. The [male] part of the body corresponds to this great earth. And also, from its intestines (?) down to its loins is like the three earths. And also, its shinbones to the pattern of the space in which the Porter stands. Its footsoles to the great earth upon which the Porter is stood; and the four fastenings that are under his feet. Its liver to the vessel of fire. Its flesh to the vessel of darkness. Its blood to the vessel of water.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic body-cosmos mapping traversing from head to feet, then internal organs. Every mapping: body part → cosmic structure. Head→garments, neck-heart→firmaments, heart→sphere, torso→atmosphere, loins→three earths, shinbones→Porter's space, footsoles→Porter's earth+fastenings, liver→fire vessel, flesh→darkness vessel, blood→water vessel. Pure substrate — both sides remain within cosmic architecture. Substrate score 18.49.

paragraphs.core_text: the small body corresponds to the macro-cosmos in its firmaments, in its orderings, in its mountains, its walls and its vessels
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Now, this is how' (bridge connective) and 'as I have made clear to you!' (first-person speaker attribution). The seam flag fired on the bridge connective but no institutional vocabulary was present — the summary content is cosmological.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary statement closing the first body-cosmos mapping section. The cosmological summary vocabulary (firmaments, orderings, mountains, walls, vessels) echoes the preceding teaching. The first-person attribution marks editorial voice.

paragraphs.core_text: There exist five great camps in this great outer zone, of which the five sons of the Living Spirit are masters.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once more, I reveal to you:' — first-person speaker attribution/frame formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces the five-watch teaching. The substantive content (five camps, five sons of the Living Spirit) defines the teaching structure — this is a cosmological question-answer unit. The frame formula is stripped but the teaching thesis preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: So, in the first watch-station above, of which the Keeper of Splendour is master, on the battlement of all the works, is found his authority over the three heavens. Then the ones below him [ ... ... ] the great King of Honour.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First in the five-fold watch enumeration. Maps first watch → Keeper of Splendour → three heavens. Lacuna present. Both sides remain within cosmic system. Substrate score 18.6.

paragraphs.core_text: The second watch, of which the great King of Honour is master, his own authority (extends) over the seven firmaments beneath him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second watch enumeration. King of Honour → seven firmaments. Highest substrate score in chapter (50.0). Pure systematic mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: The third watch, of which the Adamant [is master, his authority] reigns from the firmament down below to the [earth]. [And he] invigorates, according to his authority, the sphere and the worlds of the atmosphere; and the other four worlds that are appointed on this earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third watch enumeration. Adamant → firmament to earth, sphere, atmosphere, four worlds. Restorations in brackets. Describes cosmic process ('invigorates').

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth watch, over which the King of Glory has power, is the three wheels. And his authority lies over the three earths upon the head of the Porter.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth watch enumeration. King of Glory → three wheels → three earths above Porter. Substrate score 40.0. Pure cosmic geography.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth watch is the watch over which the Porter is authoritative. Again, he is master, according to his authority, over this great earth he stands upon, and the four fastenings under his feet.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth and final watch enumeration. Porter → great earth + four fastenings. Completes the five-fold structure. Despite 0.0 substrate vocabulary score, content is pure cosmic mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Affliction has come about in these five watches from time to time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Transitional thesis statement introducing the five cosmic conflicts. Describes cosmic-temporal process. Brief but structurally essential — opens the second teaching block within the five-watch framework.

paragraphs.core_text: So, in the watch of the Keeper of Splendour, Sin desired to spurt up towards the image of the Ambassador. Yet, they barred it from that place, and it fell back down in shame.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First cosmic conflict. Sin (capitalized as cosmic agent) acts against the Ambassador — both cosmic entities. Process description: Sin rises, is barred, falls. Both sides within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, an earthquake and treachery occurred in the watch of the great King of Honour, which the watchers who had arisen at the time and had [ ... ] they who were sent came down, until they were humbled.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second cosmic conflict. 'Watchers' (egrēgoroi) are cosmic beings in the tradition. Lacuna present. Describes cosmic upheaval and resolution. All entities remain within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, in the watch of the Adamant, the abortions came to the earth and fashioned [the] figure of flesh.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third cosmic conflict. 'Abortions' are cosmic entities (archontic offspring) in Manichaean cosmology. They fashion the body of flesh — cosmic process of embodiment. Both sides within system.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, in the watch of the King of Glory, a commotion happened in these three earths above the Porter. The pathway was obstructed for the ascent of these three wheels; that of wind, that of water, and that of fire.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth cosmic conflict. Three earths, three wheels (wind, water, fire) — systematic cosmic geography. Describes obstruction of cosmic process. Substrate score 30.0.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, in the watch of the Porter, the fastenings beneath were laid bare and strained their chains. A great earthquake befell that place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth cosmic conflict completing the enumeration. Fastenings and chains — cosmic binding structures. Pure process description.

paragraphs.core_text: [Like] these five watch-stations, which exist in this great [ ... these five] camps: this is also the case with this body. There are another five camps there, and the Light Mind is watching over them, and the new man who is with him.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'which I have recounted [to] you' (first-person speaker attribution) and 'that the elect wear' (institutional reference to Manichaean elect class).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Bridge from macrocosmic five-watch teaching to body-microcosm. The correspondence (five cosmic watches → five camps in body) is substrate. 'Light Mind' is a cosmic entity (Nous) in the emanation hierarchy. 'The new man' may be Manichaean/Pauline overlay — uncertain. Institutional score 3.7 from 'elect' reference.

paragraphs.core_text: The configuration of his face, which is above his body: the mystery of the Keeper of Splendour, who rules over the watch above the zone.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'The elect person who will control and subdue... and guide it towards the good: he resembles' — ethical application framing that wraps the body-cosmos correspondence in instructions for the elect. One side (ethical mastery of face) reaches into community practice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First in the five-fold body-ruler correspondence series (¶18-22). The substrate mapping (face ↔ Keeper of Splendour) is the only place this correspondence appears in the chapter. The 'whoever will master' framing converts impersonal correspondence into ethical application. Institutional score 4.88.

paragraphs.core_text: His heart: the sign of the great King of Honour, who subdues the seven heavens.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Whoever will become master [over]... and subdue it: he is' — ethical application framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second body-ruler correspondence. Heart ↔ King of Honour. Same ethical application pattern as ¶18.

paragraphs.core_text: His genitals: the mystery of the Adamant of Light, the one who subdues Matter.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Whoever will become master to... and subdue his lust: he is' — ethical application framing. 'Subdue his lust' is particularly clear ethical instruction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third body-ruler correspondence. Genitals ↔ Adamant of Light ↔ Matter. The substrate maps a body region to its cosmic ruler and the cosmic ruler's function (subduing Matter).

paragraphs.core_text: The stomach and the fire that is in him: the likeness of the King of Glory, the one who turns the wheels, sending the life above.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Whoever will subdue... and become master to... and also purify the nourishment that comes in to him: he resembles' — ethical application framing with specific dietary/purification instruction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth body-ruler correspondence. Stomach/fire ↔ King of Glory (wheel-turner, life-sender). The substrate describes the cosmic function: turning wheels, sending life upward — cosmic process.

paragraphs.core_text: The ruling-power that is beneath in his feet: the Porter, the one who subdues with his footsoles the abysses below.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Whoever will become master over... and bind it with the chain of peace: he is like' — ethical application framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth and final body-ruler correspondence completing the enumeration. Feet/lower power ↔ Porter subduing abysses. Parallel structure to ¶10 (macrocosmic Porter description).

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the teaching of wisdom, which circulates in that body: to the likeness of the Virgin of Light, who goes up and comes down in this zone, above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps inner wisdom circulation to Virgin of Light's movement in the cosmic zone. Both sides within the system — wisdom as cosmic faculty, Virgin of Light as cosmic entity. Body-cosmos correspondence in process mode (circulation ↔ ascent/descent).

paragraphs.core_text: love and joy, faith and truth: they are to the likeness of these two light ships. For, the living soul should go up in them and become free through them; and it ascends from the abysses below and arrives at the heights above.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Also,' (connective) and 'in which the person should live' (prescriptive ethical clause directing the person how to live).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps inner virtues (love, joy, faith, truth) to the two light ships. Soul ascent described as cosmic process. The 'should' in 'should go up' may reflect Coptic subjunctive describing the process rather than ethical command — retained as process description. The brief prescriptive 'in which the person should live' is the only clearly editorial element.

paragraphs.core_text: There exist four worlds in this body of the flesh, and there exist countless times seven rulers in the body of the four worlds!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once more, understand this other (truth):' — pedagogical address/frame formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Thesis statement opening the four-worlds-in-the-body teaching block. The numerical system (four worlds × seven rulers) is pure substrate teaching structure. Introduces ¶26-29.

paragraphs.core_text: So, the first world is from its neck up; and also the seven rulers who are in this upper world are these: the two organs of sight, and the two of hearing, and the two of smell. The other one is the mouth, which is the organ of taste.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First world enumeration: head region → seven rulers (sense organs: 2 sight + 2 hearing + 2 smell + 1 taste = 7). Pure systematic body mapping. Despite 0.0 substrate vocabulary score, content is clearly oldest layer — systematic enumeration of body-cosmos structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The second world is from its neck down to its entire upper torso. And also, the seven rulers who are in this second world are: its two arms that accord to the pattern of its two ears, which occur in its first world above; and its two breasts that are to the pattern of its organs of smell; and the two eyes of its heart; and the gullet of the stomach between the two breasts, which in the chest is the pattern of the mouth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second world enumeration: torso → seven rulers. Remarkably, each torso organ is mapped to its corresponding sense organ in the first world (arms↔ears, breasts↔nostrils, heart-eyes↔eyes, gullet↔mouth). This is body-cosmos correspondence within the body itself — degree mapping domain onto domain. Pure substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Once more, there exist seven rulers in the third world of the body, which are these: the fat, the lung, the spleen, the liver, the gall, and its two kidneys.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third world enumeration: abdominal organs. Seven rulers: fat, lung, spleen, liver, gall, 2 kidneys = 7. 'Once more' is a mild teaching connective, part of the enumeration structure. Pure substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the fourth world below. There are another seven there of this same kind: its two buttocks (?), and its two testicles, and its two loins; and the member out of which the seed comes, that begets all the forms.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth and final world enumeration completing the four-fold structure. Lower body → seven rulers: 2 buttocks + 2 testicles + 2 loins + 1 generative member = 7. 'That begets all the forms' — substrate description of cosmic-generative function.

Pure formulaic transition: 'Once more the enlightener speaks to his hearers.' Marks the seam between source blocks (four-worlds teaching → zodiac-body teaching). Gardner notes the chapter is redacted from multiple sources — this frame marks one such join.

paragraphs.core_text: Aries and Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces; these are the twelve signs of the zodiac that occur in the worlds above, on the sphere. They are interlocked and bound on this turning wheel, the one in which they are [ ... ], fixed, and planted. And, regarding all these twelve signs of the zodiac, this is how they were appointed and made leaders [ ... ] on the sphere beneath the heaven that is the wheel of the stars. Now, they are appointed like this, they are thus, so that you can find the head of [ ... ] and you find the tail too [ ... ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Lists all twelve zodiac signs and describes their cosmic placement on the sphere. Multiple lacunae. 'Head to tail' describes the zodiacal arrangement — astronomical substrate. 'You can find' is generic pedagogical address within the teaching tradition, not editorial application. Substrate score 48.28.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, they occur like this, these that we have recited, one after another in this body. They are counted by order and number from the head to the feet. Its head is Aries. Its neck and its shoulders are Taurus. Its two arms Gemini. Its upper torso is Cancer. Its stomach is Leo. Its belly is Virgo. The vertical spine and its intestines (?) are Libra. Its genitals Scorpio. Its loins are Sagittarius. Its knees are Capricorn. Its shinbones are Aquarius. The soles of its feet are Pisces.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Linear zodiac-body mapping, head to feet: Aries→head, Taurus→neck/shoulders, Gemini→arms, Cancer→torso, Leo→stomach, Virgo→belly, Libra→spine, Scorpio→genitals, Sagittarius→loins, Capricorn→knees, Aquarius→shinbones, Pisces→feet. Standard zodiacal melothesia — ancient body-cosmos correspondence. 'These that we have recited' is minor pedagogical self-reference within the teaching tradition. Substrate score 40.91.

paragraphs.core_text: Behold, these are also distributed one after another. They exist in this body, as if turned to the side and bent to the pattern of the twelve signs of the zodiac. They too are thus, arranged one against another, head to tail, as they occur on the wheel [ ... ] up.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces the second zodiac-body schema (circular/lateral arrangement). 'Head to tail' astronomical terminology. 'As they occur on the wheel' — body arrangement mirrors zodiacal arrangement on the sphere. Lacuna present.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, they are counted by order and number of the body and all its members. So, we have proclaimed that these are turned to the side, bent, and spread out; because from its head down to its hip shall count six to its left, and another six to its right.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explains the lateral distribution: six zodiac signs on the right side, six on the left. 'We have proclaimed' is minor pedagogical self-reference, part of the teaching voice. The structural principle (6 right + 6 left) is substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The six that are down its right are these: the right temple is Aries; its right shoulder is Taurus; its right arm is Gemini; its right rib-cage is Cancer; its stomach is Leo; the right side of its reproductive organs are Virgo.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'that I will recount' — first-person speaker attribution within the introductory clause.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Right-side zodiac-body mapping: Aries→right temple, Taurus→right shoulder, Gemini→right arm, Cancer→right rib-cage, Leo→stomach, Virgo→right reproductive organs. Pure zodiacal melothesia in lateral schema. Substrate score 38.3.

paragraphs.core_text: the other six which are to its left, in contrast they come from its hip to its head: its left [ ... ] is Libra; its left rib-cage is Scorpio; its left breast and left kidney is Sagittarius; its [left] elbow is Capricorn; its left shoulder is Aquarius; its left temple is Pisces. This is how the creator of the body himself has appointed them. He has [set] them in order and arranged them, one against its companion, head to tail.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Conversely,' and 'about which we have spoken,' — editorial self-reference phrases.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Left-side zodiac-body mapping completing the circular schema: Libra→left [...], Scorpio→left rib-cage, Sagittarius→left breast/kidney, Capricorn→left elbow, Aquarius→left shoulder, Pisces→left temple. 'The creator of the body' — refers to the archontic craftsman who structured the body; cosmic agent, not editorial reference. 'Head to tail' is astronomical-structural terminology. Lacuna and restoration present.
Minimal formulaic transition: 'Once more he speaks.' Marks another source seam — transition to the rulers/illness teaching block.

paragraphs.core_text: There exist many powers in this body. They are the house-dwellers who are made the leaders in it. There are eight hundred and forty times ten thousand rulers made chiefs in the human body! They are distributed and set firm, quartered according to house. The count and number of their houses is two hundred and ten times ten thousand.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Listen to this other lesson that I will proclaim to you. Understand that' — speaker address and frame formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numerical body-cosmos teaching: 8,400,000 rulers in 2,100,000 houses within the body. 'House-dwellers' and 'quartered according to house' — cosmic-architectural vocabulary describing the body's internal structure. The precise large numbers are characteristic of the substrate's systematic-enumerative style.

paragraphs.core_text: When all these rulers come creeping and moving within the body, they will meet one another; and they shall beset and destroy one another, and [ ... ] in them there. When [ ... t/il]] they shall erupt from the body of the person who [will] die; and make putrid boils and sores and burning wounds in the body. Either they might have made him sick within; or else they might come forth upon his outer side. Those wounds shall first be squeezed and discharge their liquid, and empty out their pus, until they are squeezed [ ... ... ] and the suppuration forced out from the wound. Afterwards, their scars shall close over; and they are healed and obtain relief from the places that came out upon them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process description: cosmic rulers within the body conflict, causing illness and suppuration. Describes the natural process of wound formation and healing as a function of inner-ruler activity. Pure body-cosmos process — both sides (rulers, bodily manifestation) stay within the system. No ethical application, no contemporary reference. Multiple lacunae. The detailed natural-process observation (pus discharge, scar closure, healing) is characteristic of the substrate's descriptive voice.
